title: Calculate ballast weight shift and required weight location
subject: General
assumptions: If no value is given, the weight is traced to the Aircraft Specifications or TCDS and that source is cited.
The weight used does not exceed the maximum allowable gross weight for the category being computed.
The stated direction of required CG shift matches which limit was exceeded (aft-out CG requires forward shift).
The CG limits used match the published/given range for the applicable category rather than an assumed value.
The recorded arm carries the correct algebraic sign relative to the aircraft datum used in the problem.
The chosen ballast station lies on the side of the CG that moves the CG toward the exceeded limit.
openQuestions: Every check, error mode and evidence item in this pack was drafted by packs/compile_pack.py from the procedure sheet and handbook, and has not been reviewed by a subject-matter expert.

Confirm the governing reference. FAA-H-8083-30B pp. 6-3 to 6-6 was located during compilation and is not cited by the procedure sheet; an SME must confirm it, or supply the correct citation, before this pack is marked reviewed. Note that the extract given covers CG, datum, and empty weight but contains no ballast-shift formula.

Is the recomputation of loaded CG with ballast installed in scope? It is not in the four step instructions but appears in the step-level checks; if out of scope, evidence item 5 and the corresponding criterion line must be dropped.

Do the instructor-issued problem sets state the datum location and sign convention, or is the student expected to assume a positive-aft arm? This determines whether the algebraic-sign criterion is fair.
Is the maximum-allowable-gross-weight check taught in this task or in a separate weight-check task?
Is permanent ballast (approval, placarding, permanent installation) assessed anywhere, or does the sheet's mention of it remain background only?

checks.text: The weight entered is the aircraft's total (loaded) weight from the given problem data, not the empty weight.
checks.src: Formula uses 'total acft weight'; note 1 gives it as a supplied value, e.g., 2,500 LBS.

checks.text: The total weight figure is legibly recorded on the worksheet with pound units shown.
checks.src: Step 1 requires the value be identified and carried into the ballast formula; units make it auditable.

checks.text: If no value is given, the weight is traced to the Aircraft Specifications or TCDS and that source is cited.
checks.src: Handbook: maximum weight 'is indicated in the Aircraft Specifications or TCDS'; reference is uncited/provisional, needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: The weight used does not exceed the maximum allowable gross weight for the category being computed.
checks.src: Handbook: 'variations to the maximum allowable weight depending on the purpose and conditions'; provisional, uncited reference needing SME confirmation.

errors.text: Empty weight substituted for total loaded weight, producing a plausible but understated ballast figure.
Given weight transcribed incorrectly (digit or decimal error) into the formula.
Value written without units or unlabeled, so its role in the formula is ambiguous.

steps.text: Identify how far CG is out of range.

checks.text: The out-of-range distance is computed against the nearest exceeded CG limit, not the opposite limit (e.g., 71.2" − 70" = 1.2").
checks.src: Procedure sheet note 2: "When shifting CG, shift it to the closest limit it currently is out of."

checks.text: The stated direction of required CG shift matches which limit was exceeded (aft-out CG requires forward shift).
checks.src: Handbook: "Weight being added forward of the datum produces a negative moment"; sign/direction logic. Assumed reference — needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: The CG limits used match the published/given range for the applicable category rather than an assumed value.
checks.src: Handbook: specifications "furnished by the FAA ... in the TCDS or Aircraft Specifications." Assumed reference — requires SME confirmation.

checks.text: Written solution legibly shows the given CG range, current CG, and the subtraction, with inch units labeled.
checks.src: Procedure sheet gives worked example format "64"-70"; CG @ 71.2"" as the expected showing of work.

errors.text: Subtracts the far (non-exceeded) CG limit from current CG, producing a plausible but oversized shift distance.
States the shift direction backwards, so ballast would be placed on the wrong side and worsen the CG.
Omits units or mislabels the result, or arithmetic transcription is illegible.

checks.text: The worksheet records a single ballast location expressed as a fuselage station or arm in inches, not a vague area.
checks.src: Senior Mechanic Note 3: location is 'usually a baggage compartment or a given fuselage station (e.g., ballast location +45")'.

checks.text: The recorded arm carries the correct algebraic sign relative to the aircraft datum used in the problem.
checks.src: 'Whether the moment is preceded by a positive (+) or negative (−) sign depends on its location in relation to the datum'; handbook not cited, needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: The chosen ballast station lies on the side of the CG that moves the CG toward the exceeded limit.
checks.src: Sheet example places ballast at +45" to move CG forward from 71.2"; handbook: 'Weight being added forward of the datum produces a negative moment'. Handbook uncited, provisional.

checks.text: The location used is one given or approved for ballast (e.g., baggage compartment), not an arbitrary or inaccessible point.
checks.src: Note 3 restricts location to a baggage compartment or a given fuselage station.

errors.text: Ballast station chosen on the same side as the CG excess, so the computed weight would worsen the out-of-limit CG while the arithmetic still looks correct.
Arm recorded without sign or measured from the wrong reference, corrupting the ballast-to-CG distance in the formula.
Location written without units or station label, or as a general area rather than a numeric station.

checks.text: The denominator is the distance from the ballast station to the desired CG limit (70−45=25"), not to the current CG.
checks.src: Procedure sheet formula: 'distance between ballast location and desired CG'; worked example uses (70−45).

checks.text: The computed ballast weight equals total weight × shift distance ÷ that arm (e.g., 2,500×1.2÷25 = 120 lb).
checks.src: Procedure sheet worked example: '(2,500 x 1.2) / (70-45) = 3,000 / 25 = 120 LBS'; handbook extract gives no ballast formula.

checks.text: Ballast station chosen is on the side of the CG that moves it toward the nearest exceeded limit.
checks.src: Senior Mechanic Note 2: 'shift it to the closest limit it currently is out of'; requires correct fore/aft sense.

checks.text: Recomputed loaded CG with the ballast installed falls inside the published range and total weight stays within maximum allowable.
checks.src: Handbook: 'maximum authorized weight of the aircraft and its contents'; source not cited by procedure sheet, so needs subject-matter confirmation.

errors.text: Arm taken from ballast station to current CG instead of desired limit, understating ballast so CG remains out of range.
Ballast weight applied at a station on the wrong side of the CG, driving the CG further out of limits.
Result recorded without units or station reference, or rounded down below the required weight.
